transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um... I guess the main reason I’m here is just... well, I’ve been having a little bit of trouble keeping up at work. 

I'm a registered nurse, and I really do love my job and care about my patients, but... on the floor, I seem to be losing my train of thought a lot. I know the wards are always chaotic, so maybe it's just normal stress? But if, say, an IV pump beeps in the hallway, or I hear someone asking another nurse a question, or a call light goes off... suddenly I’ve just completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was working on. 

It’s a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I don't want to sound like I'm not doing a good job. I really try my best to stay on top of everything. I hope that makes sense? Is that... is that something people usually come in to talk about?
Have you had this kind of trouble with attention or getting distracted since you were a child?

Well... yes, I suppose I have. I mean, I always just thought I was a typical kid, maybe just a little bit of a daydreamer? But... um, even back in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright—which was really nice of them to say!—but they'd also usually mention that I was... well, a bit careless. 

I was always losing my worksheets, or I'd completely forget to turn in my homework. I really wasn't trying to be difficult or a bad student, I promise. My mom actually had to sit with me every single night just to keep me on track and make sure I got things done. I always felt a little guilty about taking up so much of her time like that... 

Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Did these attention or distraction problems also happen outside of school and work, such as at home or in other activities?

Um... yes, I guess they do happen outside of work, too. I mean, I try really hard to keep my personal life organized, I really do. But... sometimes little things slip my mind. 

Just normal, routine things, you know? Like... I might forget to call my mom back, or I'll realize I forgot to pay a bill until the last minute. Or, um, sometimes I'll completely miss a dentist appointment. It's so embarrassing when that happens, because I really didn't mean to! I even set reminders on my phone sometimes, and I still somehow manage to miss them. 

And at work, it's the same kind of thing... like forgetting to follow up on a missing lab order, even though I knew I needed to do it. I just... I don't want you to think I'm irresponsible or that I don't care about these things. I really try to be on top of it all. I just... I don't know why it keeps happening. Am I explaining that right? Is that helpful at all?
Did you also have a lot of fidgeting, restlessness, or difficulty sitting still when you were a child?

Oh, um... no, not really. I don't think so, anyway. I was actually a very quiet little girl. 

I would mostly just sit at my desk and... well, like I mentioned, just stare out the window or daydream. I never really ran around or caused trouble in class or anything like that. I always tried really hard to be good and not bother the teachers, you know? I really didn't want to be a disruption to anyone. 

So... no, sitting still wasn't really an issue for me. Is... is that okay? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you spend a lot of time feeling nervous or worrying about different things?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I guess I worry a normal amount about doing a good job? Like, being a nurse, I really, really want to make sure I'm doing right by my patients, so I care about that a lot. But... I wouldn't say I'm a naturally nervous person. 

I don't spend my days feeling anxious or on edge or anything like that. Mostly I just get frustrated with myself when I let things slip through the cracks, like I mentioned before. But actual worrying about different things... no, not really. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for.
How much are these attention problems interfering with your work or daily life?

Um... well, it's... it's been a bit difficult lately, to be completely honest. I really, really try my best every single shift, I promise I do. I care so much about my patients and my team. 

But... I guess the attention stuff is starting to cause some issues at work. It's so hard to admit this, but... they actually had to put me on formal supervision recently. And... um, when I'm acting as charge nurse, the other nurses have to double-check parts of my follow-through now. 

It just breaks my heart because I'm supposed to be a leader for them, and instead, I feel like I'm becoming a liability. I hate feeling like a burden to my coworkers when they already have so much on their plates. I'm really working on it, though, and trying to find better systems for myself! 

Is... is it okay that I'm sharing this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even though it's a little embarrassing to talk about.
